**Finding submitted: INSURANCE — missing (confidence 0.90).**

- **Investigation:** Full-document searches for "insurance", coverage/policy, certificates and workers' compensation returned no hits. The planner's candidates were checked directly: §5.3 Security only disclaims IBM's security warranties and pushes option-selection responsibility onto us; §14.12 Risk of Loss merely splits risk between Base Components and Customer Components. §14.18 confirms IBM processes personal information on our behalf, and IBM hosts the e-business Hosting Environment — so this is exactly the data-touching vendor the rule targets, and no insurance covenant exists anywhere (including Order Form / Service Option Attachment references).
- **Classification:** Missing / walk-away territory (no insurance for a vendor processing personal data), so an insert is warranted.
- **Cure:** One `insert_after` op creating new §14.21 Insurance at the end of the Notices/miscellaneous run, carrying all six preferred elements — CGL USD 1M per occurrence / USD 2M aggregate, E&O USD 2M, cyber and privacy USD 5M where IBM processes data belonging to, supplied by or processed for us (drafted broadly rather than by named data examples), statutory workers' compensation, and certificates on request. No survival tail, at-own-expense language, or other non-element boilerplate was added, and the comment offers the E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M fallback.
